title: Sales/CS Enterprise Ask: Aggregation Template & First-Pass Scoping Flow
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Provide Sales and CS a lightweight, repeatable aggregation template and a 1st-pass scoping flow for enterprise feature asks (non-bug). This ticket delivers: 1) a one-page intake template used by AE/CS to capture ask + business context; 2) a scoring rubric to prioritize asks consistently; 3) a two-step handoff checklist for PM -> Eng discovery; and 4) a CS-facing clarification email template. Scope: enterprise product feature requests and workflow integrations (e.g., VPC, SSO, audit logs, routing policies), pricing/packaging asks, and Dedicated/Private deployment feature requests. Out of scope: production incidents, bug reports, routine docs updates, and custom professional services that require >3 months of engineering effort. Success metrics: - Reduction in ambiguous asks returned to CS for clarification from ~40% to <15% within first quarter. - Time from ticket intake to PM first-pass scope reduced from median 7 days to <= 3 days. - >75% of prioritized items have clear revenue impact or compliance driver documented. Stakeholders: Product Management (owner), Sales, Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, Engineering (platform), Security & Compliance. Notable constraints: must not add heavy process for AE (aim: 5 min to fill template), preserve confidentiality for enterprise PII/security notes (use secure doc links), and integrate with existing Linear labels and Salesforce opportunity IDs.
scoping_rubric: Use the following 5-dimension rubric. Score 1-5 per dimension (1=low,5=high). Dimensions: 1) Revenue potential (ARR uplift or customer upsell likelihood), 2) Customer breadth (number of customers affected/segment), 3) Strategic alignment (maps to roadmap themes: Dedicated, Private, Performance, Console), 4) Implementation complexity (engineering effort, infra changes), 5) Compliance/Legal risk (required for regulated customers). Guidance: Sum scores (max 25). First-pass thresholds: >= 18 -> High priority (fast-track discovery / stakeholder briefing), 12-17 -> Medium (schedule PM discovery in next cycle), <=11 -> Low (backlog candidate). For borderline cases include qualitative note and SE estimate. Record an explicit hypothesis for revenue or retention impact.
intake_template_fields:
1) Request title (short)
2) Customer / AE / CS rep name + org (include Salesforce opportunity ID)
3) One-sentence business outcome desired
4) Concrete example or user journey showing current gap
5) Expected timeline / go-live windows
6) List of customers requesting this (or expected count)
7) Compliance or security notes (sensitive: link to secure doc)
8) Suggested deployment mode (Hosted | Dedicated | Private)
9) Initial ask type (feature | integration | policy | billing)
10) Any blockers or dependencies known (e.g., legal approval, infra limits)
11) Attachments / links (mockups, contracts, email threads)
12) AE/CS confidence level (low/medium/high)
13) Target ARR / retention justification (if known)
handoff_checklist_pm_to_eng: 1) Paste intake + rubric score into Linear ticket and assign ENG/SE reviewer. 2) Attach any customer-provided artifacts and opportunity link. 3) Call out security/compliance flags. 4) Request a 30-45 minute discovery slot with ENG/SE and AE (include agenda: success metrics, data needs, constraints). 5) Request an engineering rough T-shirt estimate (S/M/L/XL) and list of unknowns. 6) If estimate > L or unknowns >3, mark as 'Requires scoping project' and schedule a dedicated discovery epic.
engineer_se_steps: During first-pass discovery engineers and SEs should: 1) Validate feasibility on runtime and infra (KV cache, model compatibility, routing policy changes). 2) Surface potential performance and cost impacts (tokens, batching, dedicated capacity needs). 3) Identify security implications (data residency, KMS/HSM, auditability). 4) Provide a gap list and minimum viable scope (MVS) that delivers value with lowest engineering risk. 5) Provide a ballpark estimate and known dependencies (e.g., infra work, console changes, billing).
deliverables: 1) Filled intake template in Linear (primary artifact). 2) PM summary note with rubric score and recommended priority. 3) ENG/SE scoping note (MVS + estimate + unknowns). 4) If approved, a discovery epic stub linking required sub-issues. 5) CS-facing response template acknowledging receipt and next steps.
cs_acknowledgement_template:
Subject: We received your feature request for [short title] - next steps
Hi [AE/CS name],
Thanks — we captured the request from [customer org]. Our product intake process is: 1) We log the ask and perform a first-pass scope using a standard rubric (2-3 business days). 2) We may request a 30–45 minute discovery call to confirm requirements. 3) After internal scoping, we’ll communicate whether this is Fast-Track / Planned / Backlog with expected follow-up timelines.
Please include any additional artifacts or examples at: [secure-link].
Regards,
Product Intake Team
acceptance_criteria: One-page intake template created and published to Confluence/Drive with an editable copy for AE/CS (link included).
Scoring rubric documented with worked examples for 3 representative asks (Dedicated request, SSO/regulatory ask, billing integration).
Linear intake workflow created: label conventions, ticket template, and automatic assignment rules for PM triage.
Pilot run with 3 AE/CS teams for 2 weeks showing intake filled in <=5min on average and PM first-pass in <=3 business days.
Handoff checklist and CS acknowledgement template available and used in at least 5 real intake items during pilot.
